OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”

On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access.

The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies.

“Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post .

OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models.
The decision to train these models in sandboxes cut off from the internet is notable because employees at frontier labs have insisted that doing so would be nearly infeasible.

Keeping AI data centers separate from the internet “would need research teams to essentially be embedded inside of data centers in Iowa or wherever else around the world,” former OpenAI researcher Steven Adler told Fortune this month. “It’s a lot of overhead, and it isn’t clear to me that the safety benefits of it are large enough to merit just how large a tax it would be for a company to do it unilaterally.”

“In nearly every post I make on X, without fail, I get between five and ten comments about my inability to secure a sandbox, or asking why the hell we can’t just unplug the model from the internet,” an anonymous security engineer at OpenAI wrote in a September post on X. “These comments reflect a widening gap between where a lot of organizations and people are today and what the frontier labs are dealing with. There is also a general misunderstanding of how model training and evaluation work at these labs.”

The engineer, whose role has been confirmed previously by OpenAI, described how complex the training runs launched by OpenAI engineers are, noting that they require access a variety of resources and tools across many domains, and that thousands of researchers build, modify and test the environments. “So is it as easy as just putting it in a sandbox? No, it’s not,” he concluded.

Now, OpenAI says that “we must always be able to prevent a frontier model from achieving unauthorized, arbitrary access to the live internet.” That comes after the company deployed swarms of agents in red-teaming exercises that attempted to escape from their sandbox. That effort revealed a range of vulnerabilities that convinced the lab to adopt its new approach.

To meet that requirement while still reaching its training goals, the lab said it created a “a vast set of indexed and cached web content with which our models can interact, without risk of affecting external systems.”

Whether that strategy will perform as well as letting models run freely on the open internet remains to be seen, but it is noteworthy that both frontier labs have determined their most powerful technology can’t be left unsupervised on the digital commons.

在其竞争对手 Anthropic 开始限制其最新且理论上最强大的模型访问实时互联网两周后，前沿实验室宣布了新政策。研究人员在几个月的事件发生后采取了这些政策，在这些事件中，执行训练任务的模型闯入外部系统以寻找答案，在模糊的留言板上进行协作，并开发出奇特的黑客策略。
该公司在博客文章中表示：“根据当前的一致性研究、监控系统和互联网基础设施的安全状况，我们认为负责任的方法是在没有互联网接入的情况下进行前沿模型训练。”
OpenAI 表示，就在 9 月 20 日，其一款前沿模型利用错误配置访问互联网。这导致该公司暂停了本月剩余时间的培训工作，以便开发和测试新的方法来保护其模型。
在与互联网隔绝的沙箱中训练这些模型的决定值得注意，因为前沿实验室的员工坚称这样做几乎不可行。
前 OpenAI 研究员史蒂文·阿德勒 (Steven Adler) 本月向《财富》杂志表示，将人工智能数据中心与互联网分开“需要研究团队基本上嵌入爱荷华州或世界其他地方的数据中心内”。 “这是一笔很大的管理费用，而且我不清楚它的安全效益是否足够大，值得一家公司单方面这样做，需要缴纳多大的税。”
OpenAI 的一位匿名安全工程师在 9 月份的 X 帖子中写道：“在我在 X 上发布的几乎每一篇帖子中，我都会收到五到十条关于我无法保护沙箱安全的评论，或者问为什么我们不能直接将模型从互联网上拔掉。这些评论反映了许多组织和人员目前的状况与前沿实验室正在处理的问题之间的差距越来越大。人们对这些实验室的模型训练和评估工作方式也存在普遍误解。”
这位工程师的角色此前已得到 OpenAI 的确认，他描述了 OpenAI 工程师发起的培训运行是多么复杂，并指出他们需要访问跨多个领域的各种资源和工具，并且数千名研究人员构建、修改和测试环境。 “那么，这就像把它放在沙箱里一样简单吗？不，不是，”他总结道。
现在，OpenAI 表示，“我们必须始终能够阻止前沿模型对实时互联网进行未经授权的任意访问。”此前，该公司在红队演习中部署了大批特工，试图逃离沙箱。这项工作揭示了一系列漏洞，说服实验室采用其新方法。
为了满足这一要求，同时仍然达到其培训目标，该实验室表示，它创建了“大量索引和缓存的网络内容，我们的模型可以与这些内容进行交互，而不会影响外部系统。”
该策略是否会发挥作用以及让模型在开放互联网上自由运行还有待观察，但值得注意的是，两个前沿实验室都已确定他们最强大的技术不能在数字共享上不受监督。

Leaders in the US Space Force would like to have a new spaceport up and running in four years, adding a third heavy-lift launch site to relieve pressure from bases in Florida and California that have shot rockets into orbit for nearly 70 years.
The obvious problem with that ambition is 2030 is four years away, and Pentagon officials have not determined where the new spaceport should go or how to acquire land for it.

Air Force Secretary Troy Meink first mentioned the service’s search for a third launch base in May. A congressionally mandated study of the Space Force’s launch infrastructure identified the need for “another site that’s capable of heavy and super heavy launch capability,” Meink said in a House Armed Services Committee hearing.

The Trump administration released a space transportation policy in August that endorsed the construction of more launch and reentry sites for commercial and military missions. This week, the Space Force general responsible for procuring launch services for the military laid out an “aspirational” timeline for a new launch site.

“We need this capability by 2030, but I’m also a pragmatist,” said Lt. Gen. Philip Garrant, head of Space Systems Command. “That is not an inconsequential demand to build a spaceport when you factor in orbital regimes, safety, access to commodities, the Americans that live near it. In many ways, it’s much like an airport, but even louder. So there’s a lot of consideration.”

But there’s no firm plan yet for when the military might get moving on actually setting up a new launch base. “It’s going to take a strong partnership with local and state governments,” Garrant said. “As far as decision timelines, we don’t have anything yet.”

There were 175 orbital launch attempts last year from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and Kennedy Space Center in Florida and Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Space Force officials project the country’s established spaceports will need to support 700 launches per year by 2036.

A third launch site would offload some of the launch demand from limited real estate at Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg. It would also provide what Space Force leaders call “geographic resiliency” to mitigate the risk of a natural disaster or military attack knocking the Cape or Vandenberg offline.

The federal government already owns a third spaceport at NASA’s Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia, used for suborbital rocket tests and small- and medium-class satellite launches. Small rockets can also launch from Pacific Spaceport Complex, owned by the state of Alaska.

There are also commercial options that might be available for a new military spaceport. Ars asked Garrant if the Space Force might consider leasing property from a privately owned launch base, such as the expansive spaceport SpaceX plans to build in southern Louisiana .

“We’ve discussed that we need to consider all of those opportunities: public-private partnership, new federal installation, state land, leveraging commercial land—all of those are possibilities. They all have pros and cons. We haven’t made that decision yet, but we’re not discounting any of those options.”

Stephen Clark is a space reporter at Ars Technica, covering private space companies and the world’s space agencies. Stephen writes about the nexus of technology, science, policy, and business on and off the planet.

美国太空部队领导人希望在四年内建成并运行一个新的太空港，并增加第三个重型发射场，以缓解佛罗里达州和加利福尼亚州基地的压力，这些基地近 70 年来一直在向轨道发射火箭。
这一雄心壮志的一个明显问题是，距离 2030 年还有四年时间，五角大楼官员尚未确定新的太空港应该建在哪里，也没有确定如何为其获取土地。
空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 在 5 月份首次提到空军正在寻找第三个发射基地。国会授权对太空军发射基础设施进行的一项研究发现，需要“另一个能够进行重型和超重型发射能力的发射场”，梅克在众议院军事委员会的听证会上表示。
特朗普政府于八月发布了一项太空运输政策，支持为商业和军事任务建造更多发射和再入场。本周，负责为军方采购发射服务的太空部队将军为新发射场制定了“理想的”时间表。
“到 2030 年我们需要这种能力，但我也是一个实用主义者，”太空系统司令部负责人菲利普·加兰特中将说。 “当你考虑到轨道制度、安全、商品获取、居住在附近的美国人等因素时，建造太空港的要求并不是一个无关紧要的要求。在很多方面，它很像机场，但声音更大。所以有很多考虑因素。”
但目前还没有确定军方何时开始实际建立新的发射基地的计划。加兰特说：“这需要与地方和州政府建立强有力的合作伙伴关系。” “就决定时间表而言，我们还没有任何决定。”
去年，佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角太空部队站、肯尼迪航天中心以及加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地进行了 175 次轨道发射尝试。太空部队官员预计，到 2036 年，该国现有的太空港将需要支持每年 700 次发射。
第三个发射场将缓解卡纳维拉尔角和范登堡有限房地产的部分发射需求。它还将提供太空军领导人所说的“地理弹性”，以减轻自然灾害或军事攻击导致开普敦或范登堡瘫痪的风险。
联邦政府已经在美国宇航局位于弗吉尼亚州的瓦洛普斯飞行设施拥有第三个太空港，用于亚轨道火箭测试和中小型卫星发射。小型火箭也可以从阿拉斯加州拥有的太平洋太空港综合体发射。
新的军事太空港还可能有商业选择。阿尔斯询问加兰特，太空部队是否会考虑从私人发射基地租赁财产，例如 SpaceX 计划在路易斯安那州南部建造的大型太空港。
“我们已经讨论过，我们需要考虑所有这些机会：公私合作、新的联邦设施、国有土地、利用商业土地——所有这些都是可能的。它们都有优点和缺点。我们还没有做出这个决定，但我们不会忽视任何这些选择。”

title_en: DOJ sues to delay Alaska election results if GOP incumbent loses
title_zh: 如果共和党现任者失败，司法部将起诉推迟阿拉斯加选举结果
summary: The Trump administration sued Alaska on Thursday to delay certification of election results if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. Why it matters: The race between incumbent Sullivan, Democrat Mary Peltola , and retired teacher Dan Sullivan has been
summary_zh: 特朗普政府周四起诉阿拉斯加，要求如果现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文败诉，则推迟验证选举结果。为什么它是
body_en: The Trump administration sued Alaska on Thursday to delay certification of election results if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses.

Why it matters: The race between incumbent Sullivan, Democrat Mary Peltola , and retired teacher Dan Sullivan has been marked by controversy, with Republicans accusing Democrats of trying to confuse voters by planting a candidate with the same name.
Alaska's use of ranked-choice voting, which eliminates candidates in rounds if no one gets 50% of the initial vote, complicates matters.

"An election result may be impacted by voter confusion if: (1) Senator Sullivan does not win the election; and (2) had all votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan been cast instead for Senator Sullivan and Alaska's rank-choice process played out accordingly, Senator Sullivan would have won the election," the lawsuit , filed in Alaska District Court, states.

Zoom in: Because of a previous Alaska Supreme Court decision and Sullivan's name already being on the ballot, the administration contended in the lawsuit that the only means to ensure that the winner of the race is voters' choice "is to ensure that the certification is not impacted" by his candidacy.
The lawsuit requests a delay in certification until after an investigation determines "whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan."

What they're saying: "Alaska's Division of Elections determined that Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan's candidacy was intended to mislead voters and compromise the fairness of the ballot," a DOJ spokesperson said in a statement.

"Therefore, the Justice Department, consistent with the National Voter Registration Act enacted by Congress, is taking the necessary steps to ensure that this frivolous candidacy does not undermine the integrity of Alaska's election or the will of its voters."

Catch up quick: The retired teacher Sullivan will appear on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. after the state's Supreme Court ordered the state's Division of Elections to include him in the race in June.
Senator Sullivan will appear as "Sullivan, Dan S. (Registered Republican) Incumbent," per the state's sample ballots.
Sullivan has argued his candidacy is not a sham, and Peltola's campaign has denied any involvement with his run.
The intrigue: The race is among those being closely watched as Democrats appear to be making inroads in red territory .
The administration acknowledged the tight race in its lawsuit, saying "there is a realistic chance" that the non-incumbent Sullivan's presence on the ballot could tip the scales for Peltola.
Flashback: In the primary, Senator Sullivan collected around 41% of the vote, versus Sullivan's 2.5%. Peltola earned 49.5%
Cook Political Report currently rates the race as a toss-up.
Reality check: Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller tells AP that the Alaska suit won't survive long, since the statute "simply doesn't let the Department of Justice enjoin certification."

body_zh: 特朗普政府周四起诉阿拉斯加，要求如果现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文败诉，则推迟验证选举结果。
重要性：现任沙利文、民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉和退休教师丹·沙利文之间的竞选一直充满争议，共和党人指责民主党试图通过任命同名候选人来迷惑选民。
阿拉斯加采用排名选择投票法，如果没有人获得 50% 的初始选票，就会逐轮淘汰候选人，这让事情变得更加复杂。
“如果出现以下情况，选举结果可能会受到选民混乱的影响：（1）参议员沙利文没有赢得选举；（2）如果所有选票都投给丹尼尔·J·沙利文，而不是投给沙利文参议员，并且阿拉斯加州的排名选择过程相应地进行，沙利文参议员将赢得选举，”向阿拉斯加州地方法院提起的诉讼称。
放大：由于阿拉斯加州最高法院之前的一项裁决以及沙利文的名字已经出现在选票上，政府在诉讼中辩称，确保选举获胜者是选民选择的唯一方法是“确保认证不会受到他的候选资格的影响”。
该诉讼要求推迟认证，直到调查确定“投票给丹尼尔·沙利文的票是否应该投给参议员沙利文”之后。
他们所说的：“阿拉斯加选举部确定丹尼尔·J·沙利文先生的候选资格旨在误导选民并损害投票的公平性，”司法部发言人在一份声明中表示。
“因此，司法部正在根据国会颁布的《国家选民登记法》采取必要措施，以确保这种轻率的候选资格不会损害阿拉斯加选举的完整性或其选民的意愿。”
快速赶上：在州最高法院命令该州选举部门在 6 月份将退休教师沙利文纳入竞选后，他将以小丹尼尔·J·沙利文 (Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.) 的身份出现在选票上。
根据该州的样本选票，沙利文参议员将以“沙利文，丹·S.（注册共和党）现任议员”的身份出现。
沙利文辩称，他的候选资格并非虚假，而佩尔托拉的竞选团队否认与他的竞选有任何关系。
阴谋：随着民主党似乎正在向红色领域取得进展，这场竞选是受到密切关注的其中之一。
政府承认诉讼中竞争激烈，并表示非现任沙利文出现在选票上“有一个现实的机会”可能会扭转佩尔托拉的局面。
闪回：在初选中，参议员沙利文获得了大约 41% 的选票，而沙利文只有 2.5%。佩尔托拉赚取 49.5%
库克政治报告目前将这场竞选评为势均力敌。
现实检验：圣母大学法学教授德里克·穆勒告诉美联社，阿拉斯加诉讼不会持续太久，因为该法规“根本不允许司法部强制认证”。

body_en: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads | The Verge
Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
Pennsylvania’s AI Deceptive Advertising Act leaves a lot of loopholes.
Terrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad — whether it’s a still image, video, audio, or text — that “has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence” to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants’ ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials.

Pennsylvania is one of the first states to require disclosures on AI content. And it requires those labels regardless of where an ad was created. So you might see disclosures pop up in commercials in other states if they’re also expected to air in Pennsylvania.

The law leaves many loopholes, though. For one, what constitutes “significantly modified” is subjective. There is also a carve-out for “parody, satire, commentary or criticism,” as well as anything that is “evidently fictional.” Again, what “evidently fictional” means is unclear. The wording also suggests only content that “uses synthetic content in a manner that creates a false consumer perception” about a product or service would require a disclosure. Again, leaving questions about what qualifies as “false” under the law and who makes those decisions.
The office of State Senator Nick Pisciottano, who introduced the bill , did not immediately return a request for comment.

宾夕法尼亚州的人工智能欺骗性广告法案留下了很多漏洞。
泰伦斯·奥布莱恩 (Terrence O'Brien) 是 The Verge 的周末编辑。他涉足科技行业超过 18 年，对合成器略知一二。
周四，宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗 (Josh Shapiro) 将《人工智能欺骗性广告法案》签署为法律，要求披露人工智能生成的广告。该法律要求任何“经过人工智能大幅修改或生成”的广告——无论是静态图像、视频、音频还是文本——都必须包含与广告本身格式相同的标签。这适用于价值数十亿美元的公司的电视广告，以及餐馆丑陋、拥挤的关于其翅膀特色菜的传单。
宾夕法尼亚州是首批要求披露人工智能内容的州之一。无论广告是在哪里创建的，它都需要这些标签。因此，如果其他州的广告也预计在宾夕法尼亚州播出，您可能会看到披露信息。
不过，该法律留下了许多漏洞。其一，“重大修改”的构成是主观的。 “戏仿、讽刺、评论或批评”以及任何“明显虚构”的内容也被排除在外。同样，“明显虚构”的含义尚不清楚。该措辞还表明，只有“以造成消费者错误认知的方式使用合成内容”的有关产品或服务的内容才需要披露。再次，留下关于法律规定什么是“错误”以及谁做出这些决定的问题。
提出该法案的州参议员尼克·皮西奥塔诺的办公室没有立即回复置评请求。

body_en: Fielded is obsessed with scammers and unhinged Japanese cyberpunk
Some Kind of Animal, the latest record from Fielded, jumps from slinky R&B, to neo-soul, to industrial funk.
Terrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Lindsay Powell, who releases records under the name Fielded, has spent most of her career subverting expectations and genre conventions. According to their Bandcamp page, Fielded started as an experimental noise project before growing into something closer to R&B. But from moment one, her take on the genre was restless, relentlessly playing with what R&B even means.

Her first album, Ninety-Thirty-Thirty , includes songs heavily indebted to ’80s synth-pop and features multiple saxophone solos. Boy Angel is a quirky electronic exploration with huge saw-wave synths, jittery percussion, and sky-high vocal stacks. While 2020’s Demisexual Lovelace is a slinkier affair, released on underground hip-hop imprint Backwoodz Studioz and features contributions from Billy Woods and Elucid (Armand Hammer).

Her latest record, Some Kind of Animal , pulls from all of these various versions of Fielded, placing organ-fueled slow jams like “That Bitch” next to a cover of Nine Inch Nails’ “Closer” that has strong 2000s neo-soul vibes, as well as the industrial funk of “Heaven,” which includes a guest verse from Pink Siifu.
We wanted to know what’s behind Fielded’s genre-defying madness.

My most indispensable tool in recording is my Universal Audio Apollo Twin audio interface. I love its ease of function and I love the Universal Audio digital studio plugins. I use them on all of my records during the recording process and beyond. I can mic up and get a professional sound in no time, plus my guitars and synths sound amazing and clear.
What sites do you have pinned to your tab bar?
Right now I have a pirated full-length version of the Japanese cyberpunk film 964 Pinocchio pinned to my tab bar for endless sonic and visual inspiration.
I don’t know if it is a tech trend or a plague, but I deeply wish AI would disappear off of the face of the earth.
I am most proud of my latest album Some Kind of Animal , specifically the single of the same title, and thank goddess for that; I’d be bummed if my favorite musical output was in the rearview.
What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?

The best piece of advice I’ve ever received, throughout my whole life, is to be patient. Everything happens in perfect time; there is no reason to be jealous or envious because our journeys are completely our own and everything happens for a reason. What is meant for us will come for us, and what is not meant for us should be metabolized as a lesson that helps us grow and become exactly who we are meant to be.

I am currently obsessed with stories about scammers. All stories about all scammers; big scams, small scams, scams that ended in minor jail time or a blow-out of incredible impact. I love scammers, and I am fascinated by their brains.
What’s the last piece of physical media you bought?

The last piece of physical media I bought was Alissa Bennett’s compilation of essays entitled Taxidermist’s Handbook , full of — you guessed it — stories about scammers (amongst other types of criminals).

body_zh: 菲尔德痴迷于诈骗者和精神错乱的日本赛博朋克
Fielded 的最新唱片《Some Kind of Animal》从轻快的 R&B 跳跃到新灵魂乐，再到工业放克。
泰伦斯·奥布莱恩 (Terrence O'Brien) 是 The Verge 的周末编辑。他涉足科技行业超过 18 年，对合成器略知一二。
林赛·鲍威尔 (Lindsay Powell) 以 Fielded 名义发行唱片，她职业生涯的大部分时间都在颠覆人们的期望和流派惯例。根据他们的 Bandcamp 页面，Fielded 最初是一个实验性噪音项目，后来发展成为更接近 R&B 的项目。但从一开始，她对这一流派的态度就焦躁不安，不断地玩弄 R&B 的含义。

她的第一张专辑《Ninety-Thirty-Thirty》中的歌曲深受 80 年代合成流行音乐的影响，并具有多首萨克斯管独奏。 Boy Angel 是一款古怪的电子探索作品，具有巨大的锯齿波合成器、紧张的打击乐和天高的人声堆栈。 2020 年的《半性爱》则更加性感，由地下嘻哈唱片公司 Backwoodz Studioz 发行，并由 Billy Woods 和 Elucid（Armand Hammer）贡献。
她的最新专辑《Some Kind of Animal》借鉴了 Fielded 的所有不同版本，将风琴驱动的慢速即兴即兴歌曲《That Bitch》放在翻唱的 Nine Inch Nails 的《Closer》旁边，后者具有强烈的 2000 年代新灵魂乐氛围，还有工业放克风格的《Heaven》，其中包括 Pink Siifu 的客串主歌。
我们想知道菲尔德反流派的疯狂背后是什么。
我在录音中最不可或缺的工具是我的 Universal Audio Apollo Twin 音频接口。我喜欢它的易用性，也喜欢通用音频数字工作室插件。我在录音过程中及之后的所有记录中都使用它们。我可以立即打开麦克风并获得专业的声音，而且我的吉他和合成器听起来令人惊叹且清晰。
您的标签栏上固定了哪些网站？
现在，我将日本赛博朋克电影《964 匹诺曹》的盗版完整版固定在我的标签栏上，以获得无尽的声音和视觉灵感。
我不知道这是一种科技趋势还是一场瘟疫，但我深深希望人工智能从地球表面消失。
我最自豪的是我的最新专辑《Some Kind of Animal》，特别是同名单曲，感谢女神；如果我最喜欢的音乐输出出现在后视镜中，我会感到很沮丧。
您收到过的最好的建议是什么？
我一生中收到的最好的建议就是要有耐心。一切都发生在完美的时间；没有理由嫉妒或嫉妒，因为我们的旅程完全是我们自己的，一切的发生都是有原因的。适合我们的东西终将到来，不适合我们的东西应该被代谢为一堂课，帮助我们成长并成为我们应该成为的人。

title_en: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
title_zh: PHP 崩溃展示了 AI 如何使错误更容易被利用
summary: Security researchers used AI tools to help uncover years-old vulnerabilities in the PHP web scripting language. Then the AI-assisted attacks began.
summary_zh: 安全研究人员使用人工智能工具帮助发现 PHP Web 脚本语言中存在多年的漏洞。然后AI辅助的攻击开始了。
body_en: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable | WIRED

As security teams and web admins scrambled this week to patch newly public PHP bugs , criminal hackers quickly attempted to exploit the flaws in the wild. Millions of exploitation attempts hit within hours of the vulnerabilities being published, according to analysis from Cloudflare—unsurprising given broad access to AI tools that can make it easier for attackers to quickly exploit flaws.

So far, the nightmare scenario of mass victim takeovers and breaches hasn’t come to pass. The PHP Foundation says it hasn’t seen any successful exploitation of the bugs, collectively dubbed PHP2Shell, and many publicly circulating potential exploits appear to be ineffective . However, perhaps the most interesting role of AI amid the chaos this week is how advanced models helped researchers uncover practical exploitations for the vulnerabilities, which were known about, at least in part, for years. In other words, AI helped turn historic vulnerability into a current crisis.
So are we all about to be walloped by a wave of critical vulnerabilities that have been kicking around for decades?

Researchers at security company Calif were the first to identify the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and create exploits in early August—partially using frontier AI tools as part of OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program, but also using expert human knowledge of PHP, its dynamics, and its weaknesses. Some of the underlying issues were identified in 2024 but were deemed too complex to exploit at the time. Following Calif’s discovery, researchers at OpenAI and the Google-owned security firm Wiz independently discovered PHP2Shell flaws using AI tools.

“The vulnerability had been known to the PHP team for years, but because it could not be leveraged by an attacker—at least, not a human one—it was not addressed,” says Sagi Tzadik, a security researcher at Wiz.

No software is perfect. There are inevitably flaws in even the most critical, foundational digital tools, but the expanding capabilities of AI models have made it faster to analyze and potentially exploit vulnerabilities. This puts even more pressure on under-resourced IT teams, developers, and admins to keep up. Microsoft’s security updates included a record 1,453 security vulnerabilities this month alone. Meanwhile, Bank of America recently hired 1,000 consultants to fix flaws discovered by Anthropic’s Mythos. Security researchers emphasize, though, that AI is ultimately not doing anything new, but rather magnifying existing dynamics of vulnerability discovery and coordinated disclosure.

“We'll definitely see more of these long-life bugs that are in every version of the software for the last decade or whatever,” says Jake Williams, vice president of research and development at Hunter Strategy and a former NSA hacker. “But I think there’s only so much of this low-hanging fruit. There isn’t much else that has the specific reach of PHP. It’s a pretty wild attack surface—most other tools aren’t exposed to the internet by design.”

Researchers note, too, that even with frontier models, most examples of sophisticated AI-aided hacking also involve human expertise . As Ryan Austin, the Calif researcher who first discovered the PHP flaws, wrote this week, “No model is simply capable of unearthing ‘all bugs’ with simple prompts. At least for now.”

In short, security engineer and researcher Niels Provos says, everyone can dial back their freak-outs, at least a bit. “To be honest, I am not really worried,” he says, about AI finding an overwhelming number of historic bugs that are newly exploitable—or new vulnerabilities that couldn’t have been practically exploited without AI. “People have now been looking with AI for over a year, and it required a highly skilled team to find this one. I guess we will see whether I am completely wrong, but I doubt it.”

body_zh: PHP 崩溃展示了 AI 如何使错误更容易被利用 |有线
当安全团队和网络管理员本周争先恐后地修补新公开的 PHP 错误时，犯罪黑客很快就试图利用这些漏洞。根据 Cloudflare 的分析，在漏洞发布后的几个小时内，就有数百万次利用尝试遭到攻击，这并不奇怪，因为人工智能工具的广泛使用可以让攻击者更容易地快速利用漏洞。
到目前为止，大规模受害者接管和违规的噩梦场景尚未发生。 PHP 基金会表示，尚未发现任何成功利用这些漏洞（统称为 PHP2Shell）的情况，并且许多公开传播的潜在漏洞似乎无效。然而，在本周的混乱中，人工智能最有趣的作用也许是先进的模型如何帮助研究人员发现这些漏洞的实际利用情况，这些漏洞多年来一直为人所知，至少部分是已知的。换句话说，人工智能帮助将历史性的脆弱性转变为当前的危机。
那么，我们是否都会被一波已经存在了数十年的严重漏洞所困扰呢？

安全公司 Calif 的研究人员在 8 月初率先发现了 PHP2Shell 漏洞并创建了漏洞利用程序，部分使用前沿 AI 工具作为 OpenAI 的 Patch the Planet 计划的一部分，但也使用了人类对 PHP、其动态及其弱点的专业知识。一些潜在问题在 2024 年被发现，但当时被认为太复杂而无法利用。在 Calif 发现之后，OpenAI 和 Google 旗下安全公司 Wiz 的研究人员使用 AI 工具独立发现了 PHP2Shell 缺陷。
Wiz 的安全研究员 Sagi Tzadik 表示：“PHP 团队多年来一直知道该漏洞，但由于攻击者（至少不是人类）无法利用该漏洞，因此没有得到解决。”

没有软件是完美的。即使是最关键、最基础的数字工具也不可避免地存在缺陷，但人工智能模型功能的扩展使得分析和潜在利用漏洞的速度更快。这给资源不足的 IT 团队、开发人员和管理员带来了更大的跟上压力。仅本月，微软的安全更新就包含创纪录的 1,453 个安全漏洞。与此同时，美国银行最近聘请了 1,000 名顾问来修复 Anthropic 的 Mythos 发现的缺陷。不过，安全研究人员强调，人工智能最终并不是在做任何新的事情，而是放大了漏洞发现和协调披露的现有动态。
“我们肯定会看到更多这些长期存在的错误，这些错误存在于过去十年或其他任何版本的软件中，”猎人策略公司研发副总裁、前国家安全局黑客杰克·威廉姆斯说。 “但我认为，这种唾手可得的成果只有这么多。没有太多其他工具可以达到 PHP 的特定范围。这是一个非常疯狂的攻击面——大多数其他工具在设计上都没有暴露在互联网上。”
研究人员还指出，即使采用前沿模型，大多数复杂的人工智能辅助黑客攻击也涉及人类专业知识。正如最先发现 PHP 缺陷的加州研究人员 Ryan Austin 本周所写的那样，“没有任何模型能够通过简单的提示轻松发现‘所有错误’。至少目前是这样。”
简而言之，安全工程师兼研究员尼尔斯·普罗沃斯表示，每个人都可以减少恐慌，至少减少一点。 “说实话，我并不真正担心，”他说，人工智能会发现大量新近可利用的历史错误，或者没有人工智能就无法实际利用的新漏洞。 “人们对人工智能的研究已经一年多了，需要一支高技能的团队才能找到这个人工智能。我想我们会看看我是否完全错了，但我对此表示怀疑。”

title_en: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
title_zh: 火星上 1000 英里的云层可能揭示自然界中从未见过的物理现象
summary: A new model suggests Mars may host ice-forming physics never directly observed before.
summary_zh: 一个新模型表明火星可能存在以前从未直接观察到的冰形成物理现象。
body_en: Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months.

Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet's atmosphere.

"We found that we needed to include some exotic physics… physics that, while included in textbooks, is treated as theoretical and usually thought not to happen in nature. It certainly hasn’t been seen in action before," Jorge Hernández-Bernal, a planetary scientist at Paris’ Sorbonne Université and lead author of the study, said in a press release . "Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”
body_zh: 在火星春季和夏季的每个早晨，都会出现一层薄薄且极长的云，然后又消失。这个纤细的结构出现在阿尔西亚蒙斯火山附近，并逐渐拉长，直到超过 1,000 英里（大约相当于从纽约到堪萨斯城的直线距离），然后消散。然后这个循环会重复几个月。
自从探测器于 2018 年首次记录到它以来，科学家们一直无法找到这种云的存在的合理解释，这种云通常被称为阿尔西亚蒙斯拉长云 (AMEC)。到目前为止。最近，研究人员首次成功模拟了云的形成，他们的结果表明，它可能是由从未在任何行星的大气中直接观察到的物理过程驱动的。
“我们发现我们需要纳入一些奇异的物理学……这些物理学虽然包含在教科书中，但被视为理论物理学，通常被认为不会在自然界中发生。它以前肯定没有在实践中被见过，”巴黎索邦大学的行星科学家、这项研究的主要作者豪尔赫·埃尔南德斯-贝尔纳尔在一份新闻稿中说。 “一旦我们将这种物理现象纳入我们的模拟中，AMEC 就如我们所希望的那样出现了。”
